text:
this file defines the physical objects for one button, and the python script copies it into a three by three grid.

<highlight box="517,142,1060,175"/>up top are the simulation settings: radians for angles, a two millisecond timestep, and the solver options.

<circle box="517,176,1250,310"/>then the asset block, which is just materials: colors and shininess for the white box, black base, metal ring, stem, and the button in its off and on states. the on state glows a bit.

<underline box="530,345,765,362"/>the worldbody is the actual scene. this panel body places the grid about forty two centimeters in front of the robot. <circle box="540,395,1210,462"/>inside it, three shapes build the housing: a black base, a white box, and a thin metal ring on top.

<point x="680" y="471" label="button body"/>the button itself is its own body sitting on top of that. <highlight box="555,513,1025,546"/>this slide joint is what makes it pressable. it moves straight up and down up to a centimeter, with a spring holding it up, so it takes about five newtons to push all the way.

<circle box="555,547,1230,665"/>the stem, cap, and dome make the mushroom shaped button, and that little site marks the top of the cap, handy for tracking where the gripper should press.

<clear/><circle box="517,716,1100,800"/>last, the contact section tells mujoco to ignore collisions between the box and the button, since the stem slides inside the box and would otherwise collide with it.
